payload:
CRITICAL — data/live/market.db STRUCTURAL CORRUPTION discovered live during the pdf-ocr-orientation corpus sweep (FIX-MCPSERVER-PDFOCRWORKER-OCRONEPAGE-NO-ORIENTATION-4TH-OCR-SITE follow-up). Writes to this DB are UNRELIABLE RIGHT NOW — not confirmed self-healed. Needs db-data-integrity / ops eyes before anyone else writes to it.

UPDATE (00:19:48Z, before filing): this is NOT a novel defect — it is (at minimum) the 6th documented occurrence of the already-ESCALATED recurring-bug FIX-SQLITE-DOCKER-VIRT-CORRUPTION (agent-memory project_sqlite_corruption_fix.md: 2026-04-25 root-cause/partial-fix, RECURRED 07-13, 07-30, 08-06). `pdf_extracted_text` (rootpage 96, the exact table I was writing) was ALSO one of the corrupt trees in the 07-30 recurrence (`daily_ohlcv`(59), `pdf_extracted_text`(96)+4idx, `system_logs`(132)+5idx, `cron_job_runs`(57)+1idx, `sqlite_sequence`(3)) — plausibly the same class of hazard resurfacing on the same hot DELETE+INSERT-heavy table, not proof of a new mechanism. CHECKED AND RULED OUT the specific 08-06 recurrence mechanism (Go stock-price re-arming journal_mode WAL): confirmed via `sqlite3 data/live/market.db "PRAGMA journal_mode;"` = **delete** right now, and no `-shm`/`-wal` files present — so this is not that same re-armed-WAL vector; more likely the broader host/container advisory-locking gap the original 04-25 finding described, still unresolved, now manifesting under DELETE-mode rollback-journal locking instead of WAL/SHM. RESTORE CANDIDATE ALREADY IDENTIFIED to save ops a triage step: `data/live/market.db.backup` (mtime 2026-08-25 06:30 local ≈ 2026-08-25T04:30Z, i.e. ~20h stale) — `PRAGMA quick_check` = **ok**, `daily_ohlcv` max date 2026-08-25 (plausible/current-looking). Costs of using it: loses ~20h of ALL fleet writes (not just mine) — its own `pdf_extracted_text` row count is 15763 vs the live DB's pre-incident 15887, i.e. ~124 legitimately-added rows in that window would need replay — AND it predates this entire corpus-invalidation effort, so all 5 files/12 pages I fixed today would need to be re-applied afterward (trivial replay: `bash scripts/migrations/sweep-pdf-ocr-orientation-garble.sh --apply` once the DB is healthy again, targeting just the still-affected subset). Presenting this as A candidate for the established recovery pattern (stop the writer → back up the corrupt copy first → restore from a quick_check-verified-clean copy → restart → verify by SERVING VALUE, never just the health badge) — the actual go/no-go and whether a narrower in-place `.recover` is preferable is an ops call, not mine.

ALSO ACTIONABLE, SMALL, SAFE (not yet done, flagging for whoever picks this up): every other scripts/migrations/*.ts touching market.db (run-finalize-bctc-refine.ts, dedupe-mislabeled-bctc-period.ts, carry-forward-bctc-orphaned-rows.ts, resync-watchlist-sysmap-2026-07-11.ts) carries a standard comment — "journal_mode is NOT set here (FIX-SCRIPTS-MIGRATIONS-MARKETDB-WAL-REARM-SAME-DEFECT, 2026-07-30) — market.db's journal_mode is DELETE (schema.ts's getDb(), FIX-SQLITE-JOURNALMODE...)" — that scripts/migrations/reextract-pdf-ocr-orientation.ts (and my 2 new sibling scripts) do NOT yet carry. Doc-only, no functional change; worth adding for fleet consistency once this incident is closed.

TIMELINE (all times UTC, verified via `date -u`):
- 00:03:09 — started scripts/migrations/sweep-pdf-ocr-orientation-garble.sh --apply (79-file/312-page targeted --pages sweep; 2 files/3 pages already fixed pre-sweep as validation: DIG_2024_Q4.pdf p33, HSG_2026_Q1.pdf p4+p25 — both clean).
- Files #1, #2 (20250324-DBC..., 20250326-DIG-BCTC-hop-nhat-kiem-toan-nam-2024-cks.pdf) succeeded fully (4+4 pages each).
- File #3 (20250331-DXG-BCTC-rieng-kiem-toan-2024_signed.pdf): DELETEd 8 target rows, re-inserted 7, then crashed on the 8th (page 46) insert: `SQLiteError: database disk image is malformed / SQLITE_CORRUPT / errno 11`.
- 74 of the sweep's 77 file-invocations then crashed the same way (1 more, file #15, 20260420-DHG-BCTC-Quy-1.2026.pdf, succeeded cleanly — the failure is INTERMITTENT, not 100% at that point).
- 17 files hit the crash AFTER their DELETE committed but BEFORE all target-page re-inserts completed, leaving 28 pages with ZERO rows in pdf_extracted_text right now (previously present, garbled, now ABSENT — a real regression, worse than the pre-sweep state). Full missing list below.
- The other 57 crashed-and-continued files never reached DELETE (crashed on the DELETE statement itself or earlier) — those files' target pages are UNCHANGED from their original garbled state, confirmed by direct query against a pre-sweep manifest.
- Sweep loop finished (by design — it logs+continues on a per-file crash) at 00:07:10.
- 00:07:52 — CONFIRMED the corruption is NOT scoped to my table: the LIVE mcp-server container (vn-market-intelligence-mcp-mcp-server-1, docker logs) hit the identical `SQLITE_CORRUPT`/`database disk image is malformed` error on `post_agent_signal` -> INSERT INTO agent_signals — i.e. this was an active fleet-wide production issue during my sweep window, not something confined to pdf_extracted_text.
- `PRAGMA integrity_check` direct against data/live/market.db (run twice, both real, no timeout truncation issue — output capped at SQLite's own 100-error default limit, so the true defect count is >= what's shown): `Freelist: size is 0 but should be 1` (DB-header-level defect) + hundreds of `Rowid NNNNNNNN out of order` errors, confirmed spanning TWO different tables by rootpage lookup: `pdf_extracted_text` (rootpage 96) and `intraday_foreign_flow_5m` (rootpage 180) — both show the SAME absurd rowid values (62841914/62841915/62815607), which is far too large for pdf_extracted_text's real row count (~15.8k) and consistent with a physical page being double-referenced by two unrelated b-trees (classic 'freed-but-still-live page got reused' corruption signature, matching the header's freelist-count defect).
- No new SQLITE_CORRUPT in mcp-server logs since 00:09:00 (checked again at 00:15:12 and 00:17:08) — reads on pdf_extracted_text/agent_signals/intraday_foreign_flow_5m all currently succeed (15814/142/150095 rows respectively).
- HOWEVER: at ~00:15-00:17 I attempted a narrow, low-risk repair — re-inserting the 28 missing rows verbatim from data/live/market.db.backup (a read-only, independent 19h-stale snapshot, dated 2026-08-25T06:30Z, which still had all 28 original garbled rows) to at least undo my regression back to the pre-sweep (still-garbled, but PRESENT) state. ALL 28 insert attempts failed with the identical SQLITE_CORRUPT error — 28/28, not intermittent this time. I did not retry further and made no other write attempts after that. Net effect: this restore attempt changed nothing (confirmed: pdf_extracted_text count unchanged at 15814 before and after the 28 failed attempts) but it does mean writes are NOT reliably safe right now, more consistently blocked than during the sweep itself.

ROOT CAUSE — well-evidenced hypothesis, not fully certain: data/live/market.db is bind-mounted into vn-market-intelligence-mcp-mcp-server-1 (Docker Desktop shared volume) while also being opened directly by host-side scripts (bun:sqlite, mine) at the same time. This is the documented Docker-Desktop-shared-volume SQLite corruption class — the gRPC-FUSE/virtiofs bridge does not reliably honor POSIX advisory (fcntl) locks across the host/container boundary, so two writers with SQLite's normal locking protocol can still race and corrupt the file. This matches the DB's own history: data/live/ already holds 5 distinct dated `market.db.corrupt-*`/`.pre-salvage-*`/`.salvage-attempt-failed-*` snapshots from 2026-07-19, 07-30 (x2), 08-06 — i.e. this is a RECURRING failure mode on this exact file, not a first-time event. My sweep firing many back-to-back write transactions in a ~4-minute window very likely raised collision probability with mcp-server's own concurrent traffic (confirmed concurrent: its 00:01:41 bctcPdfPull/PEK-extraction cycle, plus ongoing agent_signals writes) and is the probable proximate trigger, but the underlying broken-locking defect predates this session and is NOT specific to my script.

WHAT I DID NOT DO: no attempt to repair the corruption itself (VACUUM, .recover, restore-from-backup, or any DB-wide operation) — that decision (in particular, whether to accept ~19h of lost fleet-wide writes by restoring data/live/market.db.backup, vs. attempting an in-place `.recover`+reload, vs. some other path) needs an ops/db-data-integrity call, not a pdf-extractor one. I stopped the moment the pattern was confirmed non-random (28/28 failed) and am not making further write attempts.

NEXT-AGENT ASK: db-data-integrity (or ops) should (1) confirm whether writes are currently blocked fleet-wide or only on specific pages/tables, (2) decide the repair path, (3) if a restore-from-backup is chosen, note the 28 pages listed below would need to be RE-invalidated afterward (they are correctly garbled in the 06:30Z backup, not yet fixed) since the backup predates the orientation-fix invalidation effort entirely.

MISSING PAGES LIST (real, ground-truth-verified against the pre-sweep 79-file/312-page manifest saved before any writes — 28 pages across 17 files, currently ZERO rows in pdf_extracted_text): 20260129-DIG-BCTC-hop-nhat-quy-4-nam-2025-cks.pdf p33; 20260422-ACB-BCTC-Hop-nhat-Quy-1-nam-2026.pdf p29; 20260130-HPG-Bao-cao-tai-chinh-rieng-Cong-ty-me-va-giai-trinh-Q4.2025.pdf p20; DXG_2025_Q2.pdf p9,p28; 20250331-DXG-BCTC-rieng-kiem-toan-2024_signed.pdf p46; VJC_2024_Q4.pdf p12,p43,p50; 20250429-SHB-Bao-cao-tai-chinh-quy-1-nam-2025-Hop-nhat-Tieng-Viet.pdf p29,p39; SHB_2025_Q2.pdf p38,p39; DBC_2025_Q3.pdf p17; DXG_2024_Q2.pdf p9,p28; DGC_2025_Q1.pdf p35; VJC_2023_Q4.pdf p12,p43,p50; DIG_2023_Q4.pdf p33; DBC_2024_Q3.pdf p17; SHB_2024_Q2.pdf p38,p39; VJC_2025_Q4.pdf p12,p43,p50; DIG_2026_Q2.pdf p32.

UNRESOLVED DISCREPANCY (flagged, not investigated further — time-boxed out): pdf_extracted_text total row count dropped from 15887 (pre-sweep baseline, confirmed 3x via the detector's own 'scanned N rows' line) to 15814 as of 00:15Z — a drop of 73, of which only 28 are accounted for by my directly-traced sweep crashes. The other 45-row delta is NOT explained by anything in my sweep log and may be ordinary concurrent mcp-server write traffic on this shared live table (it ingests new BCTC PDFs continuously) OR further corruption-related loss outside my visibility — flagging for whoever picks this up rather than guessing.

CORPUS SWEEP STATUS (separate from the corruption finding — see docs/signals/20260825T235317Z-pdfocr-orientation-corpus-scope-79-files-supersedes-qa-estimate.json for the original 79/312 scope): 5 files / 12 pages conclusively fixed and verified clean (DIG_2024_Q4 p33; HSG_2026_Q1 p4,p25; 20250324-DBC... 4pp; 20250326-DIG-BCTC-hop-nhat-kiem-toan-nam-2024-cks.pdf 4pp; 20260420-DHG-BCTC-Quy-1.2026.pdf p26). 17 files / 28 pages regressed to WORSE (row now absent, see list above). 57 files / ~272 pages untouched, still garbled exactly as before. The --pages targeted-reextract code change (scripts/migrations/reextract-pdf-ocr-orientation.ts) and the two persisted helper scripts (scripts/audits/detect-pdf-ocr-orientation-garble.ts, scripts/migrations/sweep-pdf-ocr-orientation-garble.sh) are landed and validated correct in isolation — the DB corruption is an environmental hazard the sweep exposed, not a defect in that code. DO NOT re-run the sweep until the corruption question is resolved.
addendum_20260826T002346Z: SAME INCIDENT as docs/signals/marketdb-corruption-intraday-foreign-flow-5m-20260826T001354Z.json (router, filed 00:13:54Z, already committed b400cbba2 — triage as ONE row, do not mint a second). Their runtime-layer quick_check (via bun:sqlite) found 100/100 capped error lines ALL Tree 180 (intraday_foreign_flow_5m), concluding a writer-side rowid-ordering defect confined to that one table (MAX(rowid)=62841915 over 150095 rows — a real, legitimate-looking rowid for that table, not obviously a cross-table pointer defect) plus a 'poisoned connection' theory: once a connection hits SQLITE_CORRUPT on ANY table it refuses further writes regardless of table, which would explain why MY writes to the structurally-unrelated pdf_extracted_text failed intermittently (3/77 succeeded — each sweep file-invocation was a FRESH bun process/connection, so each got an independent chance to avoid the poisoned page until it didn't). DISCREPANCY TO RECONCILE, not resolved by me: my own direct-file PRAGMA integrity_check (not runtime-layer) captured ONE additional line implicating Tree 96 (pdf_extracted_text) alongside the 98 Tree-180 lines + 1 freelist-header line (101 total, capped at 100 errors + 1 header) — see scratchpad capture referenced in my notebook. Could be a genuine second-tree defect their quick_check (lighter than integrity_check) didn't surface, or a timing difference between the two independent reads, or exactly the read-inconsistency class project_sqlite_corruption_fix.md warns about for non-plain-readonly opens. Whoever owns this incident should reconcile both captures before concluding it's confined to one tree. My additional contribution beyond their report: the concrete 28-row (17-file) data-loss inventory from my sweep, confirmation this is >=6th recurrence (their note said 4th+; project_sqlite_corruption_fix.md's own log already shows 04-25/07-13/07-30/08-06 = 4 prior + this one = 5th, so '6th' in my body text above assumed pdf_extracted_text's 07-30 appearance was a distinct extra event — treat my '6th' as approximate, theirs as the more careful count), and a failed restore-attempt data point (28/28 inserts from the clean backup all rejected at ~00:16Z, i.e. writes were still unreliable ~10 min after their 00:06:08Z 'no errors after this' observation — so the poisoned-connection window may be longer-lived or reoccurring, not a one-time blip).
